decisions.question: Spec §7.3's Flutter row and Appendix A.8 name `NidanaModule`, a wrapper widget that acquires a module scope reference on mount and releases it on unmount, needs no route names and works with any router; this contract has `ModuleRoutes` and `ModuleScopeObserver` only. Decide whether v1 adds it.

options.label: Add NidanaModule as a new widget of the main library
options.consequence: Module scope binds under any router, go_router's ShellRoute included, whose nested routes carry no names a prefix matches (R8); one more declaration for nidana.flutter.1 and one more behavior (G20) for a nidana.flutter phase; seven cases.

options.label: Leave it out of v1
options.consequence: An app on go_router or any Router-based setup has no module binding unless its Navigator routes carry prefix-matchable names, which go_router's nested routes do not (R8); Spec §7.3 and Appendix A.8 list the wrapper as part of the Flutter adapter, so the package would cover only half of what the normative row names.

decisions.chosen: Add NidanaModule as a new widget of the main library
decisions.why: Spec §7.3 (normative since DEC-685) names the wrapper as one of the two Flutter bindings and Appendix A.8 lists it among the adapter's contents; Guide Appendix B.3 gives `NidanaModule(topology, child)` for Dart; Refinement 1 already sends go_router apps to implement NavigationRouter themselves, and R8 shows a prefix observer cannot see their nested routes. The intake record recommends it. The measured facts (N1 to N6, R6, R7) show the spec's claims hold on Flutter with one narrowing (maintainState false, N4), which Refinement 8 states.

decisions.question: What does NidanaModule take: its own module declaration, a ModuleScope declared elsewhere, or a ModuleRoutes?

options.label: moduleId, topologies, gracePeriod and child; declares the module on the provided bus at mount
options.consequence: Reaches the bus through the tree like every other binding (G3); several wrappers and a ModuleScopeObserver of one module share one scope through bus-api@v2 G27's idempotent declaration; a differing declaration fails at mount with ArgumentError.

options.label: A ModuleScope argument
options.consequence: Lighter, but the scope belongs to one bus while the widget sits under a BusProvider that may provide another; nothing in bus-api exposes a scope's bus to check it.

options.label: A ModuleRoutes argument
options.consequence: Reuses a type, but ModuleRoutes requires a prefix the wrapper never reads and rejects one with no segment.

decisions.chosen: moduleId, topologies, gracePeriod and child; declares the module on the provided bus at mount
decisions.why: Consistency with the contract's rule that a binding reaches its bus through the tree (G3, Spec §3.1) and with ModuleRoutes' fields; G27 already makes repeated equal declarations one scope, which is what 'in each of its pages' needs. A ModuleScope variant is listed under Not in v2. Signal that would have changed my mind: a consumer that declares modules once at bootstrap and needs the wrapper to fail when the provided bus differs.

decisions.question: What does a NidanaModule mount do when its declaration or its acquire throws (a differing declaration, an acquire before start(), a rejected activation)?

options.label: Rethrow from the mount, holding no reference
options.consequence: Same as PageScope (G8): Flutter reports the error and builds no child, so a misconfigured module fails where it is placed.

options.label: Report through FlutterError.reportError and build the child
options.consequence: Same as ModuleScopeObserver (G10), but the subtree's pages then run without their module's state and the error is easy to miss.

decisions.chosen: Rethrow from the mount, holding no reference
decisions.why: Every cause is a programming error. ModuleScopeObserver reports only because a throw from a NavigatorObserver callback locks the Navigator (DEC-252), which does not apply to a widget; PageScope rethrows. A case pins that no child is built, and a seeded defect that reports instead fails it.

decisions.question: Does a NidanaModule rebind when rebuilt with other arguments, or when its BusProvider starts providing another bus?

options.label: Bind once, at mount
options.consequence: Same rule as PageScope (G8, v1 amendment (c), nidana.flutter D10); a module changes by remounting the wrapper.

options.label: Rebind to the new arguments or bus
options.consequence: Follows a bus recreated under mounted pages, but releases and reacquires around every such rebuild and differs from PageScope.

decisions.chosen: Bind once, at mount
decisions.why: Consistency with G8 and nidana.flutter D10, whose signal (an adopter that recreates the bus under mounted pages) has not appeared. A seeded defect that rebinds fails the binds-once case.

decisions.question: Which argument checks does the NidanaModule constructor make, and which are left to bus.module at mount?

options.label: Check at construction what the arguments alone decide: empty id, no topologies, a topology not MODULE-scoped, a negative grace period
options.consequence: The error surfaces where the widget is built, as PageScope's scope check does; only a declaration that differs from an existing one is left to the mount (G27).

options.label: Leave every check to bus.module at mount
options.consequence: No duplicated checks, but a widget built in one place fails to mount in another frame.

decisions.chosen: Check at construction what the arguments alone decide: empty id, no topologies, a topology not MODULE-scoped, a negative grace period
decisions.why: Mirrors PageScope's construction-time scope check (G8); no evidence beyond that consistency.

options.label: A clause of G10
options.consequence: One module-scope guarantee, but G10's cases and the name-prefix selection mix two bindings.

decisions.why: Guarantee ids are kept where the meaning carries over (bus-api@v2 practice); a separate id lets nidana.flutter's plan place the wrapper in a phase of its own choosing. The name prefix 'G20 ' selects exactly its cases (T7).

decisions.question: Spec §3.13 and bus-api@v2 G34: a topic widget mounted during bootstrap has a subscription that start() connects, giving it the value current once the topologies are connected, while G5 and G6 say the first value causes no rebuild. What do G5 and G6 say for that subscription?

options.consequence: Simple, but renders the first frame twice for every widget mounted after start(), which Refinement 5 exists to avoid.

options.label: Keep v1's rule and document the stale frame
options.consequence: No rule change, but a widget mounted before start() shows the declared initial value while the topic holds the value a topology's connection set, until a later publish.

options.label: Reject a topic widget mounted before start()
options.consequence: Mirrors Spec §7.2's order, but goes beyond the Specification, which rejects only MODULE and PAGE activations, and breaks v1's G5 bootstrap case.

options.consequence: States the stronger property the widget already has (widened reference, own onError); no behavior change.

experiments.question: Which flutter-binding@v1 cases fail on a bus-api@v2 runtime, does each v2 change pin a behavior that a v1 runtime or a v1 adapter breaks, and does a seeded defect of each new rule fail its cases?
experiments.finding: Structure 20 guarantees, 69 cases, 2 bindings; S17 prototype 9 contracts, 0 problems; surface clean; 7 reject libraries confirmed. After: v2 runtime + adapter v2 69/69 and executor 26/26; v1 runtime 63/69 (the six cases that pin scope timing, re-activation and the bootstrap first-value rule) and 26/26. Before: 57/57 on the v1 runtime with adapter v1 and with adapter v1 plus NidanaModule alone; 55/57 on the v2 runtime with either adapter (the two G8 cases that mount a PageScope with a topology before start()); v1 runtime + adapter v2 56/57 (v1's G5 bootstrap case, by a rebuild before start()). experiments.question: When does a widget in a page, or around a nested Navigator, mount and unmount as Flutter's Navigator pushes, covers, replaces and pops routes?
experiments.finding: N1: a pushed page mounts in the next frame; covered pages stay mounted; a popped page unmounts when its exit transition ends, not at the pop. N2: pushReplacement mounts the new page, then unmounts the old once the new has entered. N3: popUntil unmounts the removed pages when the transition ends (their order varied between runs). N4: maintainState false unmounts a covered page and remounts it when uncovered. N5: a wrapper around a nested Navigator stays mounted through unnamed nested pushes, replaces and pops, and unmounts after its own route leaves. N6: a dialog or a page pushed and popped above never unmounts it.

experiments.question: Does a wrapper work under go_router 18.1.0, and which names does go_router give the routes a prefix observer would see?
experiments.finding: R6: a wrapper in a ShellRoute builder mounts on entering the shell, stays mounted across go, push and pop inside it, and unmounts on leaving. R7: go from one page to another mounts the new page a frame before the old one unmounts, with or without a 300 ms transition. R8: nested GoRoutes name their routes by their own path pattern ('cart', 'item/:id'), so a prefix observer on 'checkout' misses them.
